name: Composer Shell
description: Three-column context-engine workspace: composition-stack rail (left), active layer canvas (center, hosting swappable per-layer content), files rail (right). Rails are 0px on the cold-launch screen and reveal on first lock or advance. Layer views hosted by the canvas are out of scope.

sourceSummary.label: Rail column toggling, storyboard dispatch, DataContext construction
InkButtonStyle / LinkButtonStyle / ChatInputTextBoxStyle consumed by this surface
AmberButtonStyle / StackRowButtonStyle consumed by this surface
Commands invoked by this surface, suggestion chips
Eight layer definitions consumed by both rails

unresolved.question: Should the center column be modeled as a navigation region rather than an inline content host?
unresolved.reason: Shell.xaml and ActiveCanvas.xaml.cs both state that the center column will become a uen:Region.Attached navigation surface, and Pages plus a RouteMap are already registered, but the shipped code hosts layer canvases inline via CanvasSlot.Content. The graph models the implemented behavior only.

unresolved.question: Is AppTitleRow part of this surface or dormant scaffolding?
unresolved.reason: The control is instantiated with live ProjectName and ShowReset bindings but Visibility=Collapsed, so its Reset action is unreachable on the current surface. It is kept in the graph because the bindings and click handler are declared and functional.

unresolved.question: Do the layer title and subtitle belong to the shell header or to each layer canvas?
unresolved.reason: ActiveLayerHeader still receives Title and Subtitle DPs from ShellModel, but TitleText and SubtitleText are Collapsed with a comment that the copy now renders inside each layer's glass container. Ownership of that content is ambiguous from this surface alone.

unresolved.question: How many rows does the files rail actually render?
unresolved.reason: The class comment says nine files (eight per-layer plus prompt-context.md), the code emits Layers.All.Length + 2 = 10 rows, and README.md appears both as the Intent layer's file and as a synthesized companion, so the list likely contains a duplicate row.

unresolved.question: Are the composition-stack layer row and the files-rail file row one shared rail-row component?
unresolved.reason: Both are three-column rows (leading marker, stretching label, trailing badge) inside a 280px rail with identical spacing and mono typography, but they differ in purpose, interactivity and projection record, so they are kept as separate canonical components.
possibleValues: one canonical rail-row with two variants

unresolved.question: Should the 480ms / QuinticEase EaseOut motion pair be tokens, given the theme dictionary declares different keys?
unresolved.reason: Tokens.xaml declares Duration.Quick/Standard/Expressive/Slow and EaseOutCubic/EaseOutExpo/EaseInOutQuint, none of which match the 480ms QuinticEase EaseOut this surface declares inline at four sites. The recurrence is real but no resource key backs it.

unresolved.question: Is the rails-hidden presentation a state or the default?
unresolved.reason: Rails start at width 0 / opacity 0 / translate ±40 in markup, so hidden is the declared baseline and only the revealed presentation is modeled as a state; the canvas, by contrast, declares both dimension sets explicitly in code, so both of its presentations are modeled.
possibleValues: explicit hidden and revealed states on both rails

metadata.scope: Shell surface only. The eight per-layer views under Views/Layers are swappable content hosted by region.active-canvas.canvas-slot and are deliberately not modeled; theme dictionaries were mined only for values this surface consumes directly or through a style it uses.
metadata.canonicalInternalsPolicy: Runtime-repeated components (layer-row, file-row, locked-context-card, future-preview-card, suggestion-chip) describe their internals as properties.parts; singleton UserControls expose child nodes only for declared literal text and interactive elements.
metadata.unmodeledDeclaredResources: Phase tints, state tints, error colors, Paper3/Paper4, Ink5, Space*/Spacing* thickness scales, Duration.* and Ease* keys, and the wider type-style scale are declared in Themes but not consumed by this surface.
